lines: Four-operator FM percussion voice; every knob and CV is read at the instant a trigger arrives and held for the whole hit
Sets the pitch the hit starts at, 1V per octave over four octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Shifts the starting pitch by up to a fifth of a volt either way, about two semitones
Sets the pitch the hit sweeps to, 1V per octave over four octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Picks one of 32 sets of frequency ratios for the four operators
Picks one of 64 combinations of wavetables for the four operators
Picks one of six FM algorithms, setting which operators modulate which and which ones reach the output
Feeds operator 1 back into its own wavetable position, none of it at the bottom of its travel and all of it at the top
Sets how long operators 1 and 3 take to fade out after a trigger, 1ms at the bottom of its travel and doubling with every five per cent of the way up
Sets how long operators 2 and 4 take to fade out after a trigger, 1ms at the bottom of its travel and doubling with every five per cent of the way up
Sets how fast the pitch sweeps from the start pitch to the end pitch; below a fifth of its travel there is no sweep and the pitch stays where it starts
Attenuates and inverts the CV for the release of operators 2 and 4
Attenuates and inverts the CV for the wave combination
Attenuates and inverts the CV for the FM ratios
Adds to the starting pitch at 1V per octave, with the total clamped to four octaves either side of C4
Adds to the end pitch at 1V per octave, with the total clamped to four octaves either side of C4
Steps through the 32 ratio sets, one set per volt with its attenuverter fully up
Steps through the 64 wave combinations, one combination per volt with its attenuverter fully up
Steps through the six algorithms, one algorithm per volt
Adds to the feedback on operator 1, a fifth of the knob's range per volt
Adds to the release of operators 1 and 3, a fifth of the knob's range per volt
Adds to the release of operators 2 and 4 through its attenuverter, a fifth of the knob's range per volt at full
Adds to the pitch envelope speed, a fifth of the knob's range per volt
A rising edge fires the voice and freezes every knob and CV reading for that hit; it reads high above 2V and low below 0.4V
A trigger arriving on the same sample as the main trigger makes that hit louder and its modulation deeper
A rising edge silences the voice at once, dropping both amplitude envelopes to 0V
The voice, reaching about 3.5V, or about 6.3V on an accented hit
Menu — DC Filter removes any DC offset from the output, and is on until turned off
Menu — Speed Ramp Looping repeats the pitch envelope instead of running it once per trigger
Menu — Trigger mods index scales the depth of the FM by the height of the trigger voltage
Menu — Operators sync on trigger resets the phase of all four operators on every trigger
PSIOP.notes: The panel marks the two release knobs Release A and Release B; the maker's tooltips name them by operator pair, and the code confirms Release B is operators 1 and 3, Release A operators 2 and 4. Only the release of operators 2 and 4, the ratio CV and the wave CV pass through an attenuverter; the other CV inputs have a fixed scaling.

lines: Bit depth reducer and sample rate decimator, polyphonic, with the depth reducer's output normalled to the decimator's input
Sets the depth the signal is quantised to, 1 to 16 bits across a 10V range
Sets how many samples are held before a new one is taken, none at the bottom of its travel and 100 at the top
The signal to be quantised, clamped to the range -5V to 5V; its channel count sets the polyphony of both halves
Takes two bits off the depth setting for every volt
The signal to be decimated; with nothing patched here it takes the output of the bit depth reducer
Adds ten held samples per volt to the decimation setting
The quantised signal
The decimated signal
Planck.notes: The panel prints Bit Crush over the knob the maker's tooltip calls Sample Rate Decimation; it is the decimator, not a second bit crusher.

lines: Random clock and noise generator: a new random value is drawn on every tick of its own clock or of an external one
Sets how often a new random value is drawn, 5Hz at the bottom of its travel and about 20kHz at the top
Scales the noise and the random clock, silent at the bottom of its travel and full at the top
A rising edge draws a new random value, and patching anything here stops the internal clock
Every volt doubles the rate of the internal clock
Adds a tenth of the amplitude range per volt
Held at 10V whenever the current random value is positive and at 0V when it is not, scaled by the amplitude setting
One sample of each new random value as it is drawn, and 0V in between
The current random value, held until the next one is drawn, clamped to the range -5V to 5V
Clock divider and sequential gate, counting incoming clock pulses from 0 to 63 and then starting again; gates are 10V high and 0V low
A rising edge advances the count
A rising edge sets the count back to the start
Carries a 10V gate for one clock period in every two
Carries a 10V gate for one clock period in every four
Carries a 10V gate for one clock period in every eight
Carries a 10V gate for one clock period in every sixteen
Carries a 10V gate for one clock period in every thirty-two
Carries a 10V gate for one clock period in every sixty-four, once per pass of the counter
Carries a 10V gate for the one clock period when the count reaches that step, the eight steps taking their turn in order
Probabilistic trigger sequencer: each step fires a gate only when it wins a random draw weighted by its own knob and CV
Sets the internal clock rate, 15 BPM at the bottom of its travel and 3840 BPM at the top
Sets how many steps the sequence runs for, 1 to 16
Sets the chance that this step fires a gate, never at the bottom of its travel and always at the top
Every volt doubles the internal clock rate
A rising edge advances the sequence, and patching anything here stops the internal clock; a gate then lasts as long as the incoming pulse stays high
Adds one step to the sequence length per volt, to a limit of 32 steps
A rising edge sends the sequence back to its first step
Adds a tenth of the chance range per volt to that step's probability
Carries a 10V gate while the clock is high on that step, and only when that step won its draw
Carries a 10V gate whenever a step fires, which is the eight step gates combined
Note — with more than eight steps the sequence wraps around the eight gate outputs, so step 9 fires the same output as step 1
Sixteen-step sequencer after the ARP 1601, with two voltage outputs, three gate busses, two quantisers and its own clock
Sends that step's gate to one of the three gate busses: bus 1 with the switch up, bus 2 in the middle, bus 3 down
Sets the voltage that step sends to the sequencer output, 0-12V
Chooses how the start inputs work: Trig toggles running on each rising edge, Gate runs the sequencer only while a signal is high
Advances the sequence by one step
Chooses what a step assigned to gate bus 3 does: Skip Step passes over it, Reset sends the sequence back to step 1, and the middle position does neither
Runs and stops the sequencer
Sets the clock rate, 15 BPM at the bottom of its travel and 3840 BPM at the top
Sets how much the clock FM input changes the clock rate; at the top of its travel every volt there doubles the rate
Sets how much of each clock cycle the clock output stays high, from a twentieth of it to all of it
Sends the sequence back to step 1
Chooses between one sixteen-step sequence and two eight-step sequences running side by side, steps 1 to 8 on output A and steps 9 to 16 on output B
Chooses whether the sequence steps in order or jumps to a step picked at random on every clock pulse
Its voltage is added to both quantised outputs after quantising, which shifts both by the same amount
A rising edge advances the sequence by one step
Starts the sequencer; in Gate mode it runs only while this input is high
The voltage quantiser A works on; with nothing patched here it takes sequencer output A
The voltage quantiser B works on; with nothing patched here it takes sequencer output B
A rising edge sends the sequence back to step 1
Stops the sequencer
A rising edge toggles the sequencer between running and stopped in Trig mode, and runs it while high in Gate mode
Changes the clock rate through the FM slider; with nothing patched here it takes gate bus 1, so a step on that bus speeds the clock up
Scales the clock pulse width, 10V leaving the slider setting as it is and lower voltages narrowing the pulse towards nothing
Carries a 10V gate while the sequence is on a step assigned to gate bus 1
Carries a 10V gate while the sequence is on a step assigned to gate bus 2
Carries a 10V gate while the sequence is on a step assigned to gate bus 3
Carries 10V while the sequence is on step 1
Carries 10V when the current step is assigned to gate bus 1 and the clock is high
Quantiser A's output: the voltage fed to it is rounded down to the nearest half volt and each half volt becomes a semitone, so 12V in comes out at 2V, plus whatever the CV input adds
Quantiser B's output: the voltage fed to it is rounded down to the nearest half volt and each half volt becomes a semitone, so 12V in comes out at 2V, plus whatever the CV input adds
The internal clock at 10V, held at 0V while the sequencer is stopped
The slider voltage of the current step; in eight-step mode it carries steps 1 to 8
The slider voltage of the current step; in eight-step mode it carries steps 9 to 16
Arpanet.notes: The gate busses, the position output and the sequencer outputs keep working while the sequencer is stopped; only the clock output is held at 0V. In random mode the step is drawn from all sixteen even when the length switch is set to two eight-step sequences.

lines: Adds a fixed whole number of volts to a signal, with eight outputs offset from four volts below to four volts above it; polyphonic
The signal every output adds its own offset to
The input with 4V subtracted
The input with 3V subtracted
The input with 2V subtracted
The input with 1V subtracted
The input with 1V added
The input with 2V added
The input with 3V added
The input with 4V added
CV recording sequencer: it samples a voltage as it moves from step to step while recording, then plays the stored voltages back in order; up to 32 steps and 16 polyphonic channels
Sets how many steps the sequence runs for, 1 to 32
Sets the internal clock rate, 15 BPM at the bottom of its travel and 3840 BPM at the top
Advances the sequence by one step, sampling a voltage as it goes if recording is on
Sends the sequence back to its first step
Sets the voltage that is recorded when nothing is patched to the input, -5V to 5V
Runs and stops the sequencer, as a toggle or while held down depending on its Trig/Gate switch
Turns recording on and off, as a toggle or while held down depending on its Trig/Gate switch
Chooses how the start button and start input work: Trig toggles running on each rising edge, Gate runs the sequencer only while the signal is high
Chooses how the record button and record input work: Trig toggles recording on each rising edge, Gate records only while the signal is high
Chooses where a sampled voltage is stored: Pre puts it in the step the sequencer is leaving, Post in the step it is arriving at
Stops recording by itself as the sequence rolls over from its last step back to the first
Adds one step to the sequence length per volt
Every volt doubles the internal clock rate
The voltage sampled into each step while recording, and its channel count sets the polyphony; with nothing patched here the module records the position of its own voltage knob
A rising edge advances the sequence by one step
A rising edge sends the sequence back to its first step
Runs and stops the sequencer, toggling on a rising edge or running while high depending on the Trig/Gate switch
Turns recording on and off, toggling on a rising edge or recording while high depending on the Trig/Gate switch
The stored voltage of the current step, or the incoming voltage while recording
Menu — Polyphony Channels fixes the number of channels recorded and played back, or follows the input when left on Auto
Asymmetrical voltage processor: it cuts the signal at a threshold voltage and delays, shapes, folds and slews the part above it separately from the part below it
Sets the voltage that divides the signal into its two parts, -10V to 10V
Crossfades the main output between the untouched input and the processed signal
Attenuates and inverts the threshold CV
Removes any DC offset from the main output
Delays the part of the signal above the threshold, from 1ms up to 10 seconds, with no delay at all at the bottom of its travel
Delays the part of the signal below the threshold, from 1ms up to 10 seconds, with no delay at all at the bottom of its travel
Bends the part of the signal above the threshold, flattening it towards 0V turned one way from the centre and pushing it out towards the rails turned the other; at the centre it is unchanged
Bends the part of the signal below the threshold, flattening it towards 0V turned one way from the centre and pushing it out towards the rails turned the other; at the centre it is unchanged
Sets the level at which the part of the signal above the threshold folds back on itself, folding more the further down its travel it goes and not at all at the top
Sets the level at which the part of the signal below the threshold folds back on itself, folding more the further down its travel it goes and not at all at the top
Limits how fast the part of the signal above the threshold can change, from 100000V per second at the bottom of its travel to 0.1V per second at the top
Limits how fast the part of the signal below the threshold can change, from 100000V per second at the bottom of its travel to 0.1V per second at the top
Attenuates and inverts the CV for the control it belongs to, and passes none of it at the centre
Shifts the threshold through its attenuverter, one volt of threshold per volt at full
The signal to be cut at the threshold and processed; one channel only
Moves the wet and dry balance of the main output, a tenth of the range per volt
Adds to the delay on the part of the signal above the threshold, a tenth of the knob's range per volt at full attenuverter
Adds to the delay on the part of the signal below the threshold, a tenth of the knob's range per volt at full attenuverter
Adds to the bend on the part of the signal above the threshold, half the knob's range per volt at full attenuverter
Adds to the bend on the part of the signal below the threshold, half the knob's range per volt at full attenuverter
Adds to the fold level for the part of the signal above the threshold, a tenth of the knob's range per volt at full attenuverter
Adds to the fold level for the part of the signal below the threshold, a tenth of the knob's range per volt at full attenuverter
Adds to the slew limit on the part of the signal above the threshold, a tenth of the knob's range per volt at full attenuverter
Adds to the slew limit on the part of the signal below the threshold, a tenth of the knob's range per volt at full attenuverter
The processed part of the signal that falls below the threshold, holding the threshold voltage itself whenever the signal is above it
Both processed parts put back together, crossfaded with the dry input by the Wet/Dry knob and filtered for DC when the DC switch is on
The processed part of the signal that rises above the threshold, holding the threshold voltage itself whenever the signal is below it
Three-band crossover built from fourth-order Linkwitz-Riley filters, with a gain control on each band, a separate output for each and a combined output; polyphonic
Sets the level of the low band, silent at the bottom of its travel, 0dB at the middle and 6dB at the top
Sets the level of the mid band, silent at the bottom of its travel, 0dB at the middle and 6dB at the top
Sets the level of the high band, silent at the bottom of its travel, 0dB at the middle and 6dB at the top
Attenuates and inverts the CV for that band's gain
Sets where the low and mid bands split, 80Hz to 640Hz
Sets where the mid and high bands split, 1000Hz to 8000Hz
Changes that band's gain through its trim knob, 2V covering the whole gain range at full
Sweeps the split between the low and mid bands, 10V covering the whole range from 80Hz to 640Hz
Sweeps the split between the mid and high bands, 10V covering the whole range from 1000Hz to 8000Hz
The signal fed to all three bands, up to sixteen polyphonic channels
The low band on its own, after its gain
The mid band on its own, after its gain
The high band on its own, after its gain
The three bands summed after their gain settings
Note — nothing is filtered until at least one of the four outputs is patched
Sequenced sampler: eight slots record from the input one after another as an external clock steps through them, then play their slices back with their own gain, mute, skip and reverse settings
Runs and stops the sequencer
Empties all eight sample slots
Steps the sequence direction on to the next of forward, reverse, bouncing and random
Arms and disarms recording; while it is armed each step records into its own slot instead of playing it back
Sets the playback level of that slot, silent at the bottom of its travel and 0dB at the top
Keeps that slot out of the main output, while its own step output carries it anyway
Passes over that step as the sequence runs; a trigger aimed straight at the step plays it anyway
Plays that slot backwards, starting from the end of what was recorded
Jumps the sequence to that step and starts its slot playing, or recording when the module is armed
Sets the rise time of the envelope applied to every slot, 1ms at the bottom of its travel and doubling with every five per cent of the way up
Sets the fall time of the envelope applied to every slot, 1ms at the bottom of its travel and doubling with every five per cent of the way up; at the top it is too long to hear at all
Resamples every slot as it plays, quarter speed at the bottom of its travel, unchanged at the middle and four times speed at the top
The signal recorded into the slot of the current step while recording is armed
A rising edge moves the sequence on one step, which starts the next slot recording or playing
A rising edge runs or stops the sequencer
A rising edge empties all eight sample slots
A rising edge steps the sequence direction on to the next of forward, reverse, bouncing and random
A rising edge arms or disarms recording
A rising edge jumps the sequence to that step and starts its slot playing, or recording when the module is armed
Carries that slot's playback at its own gain, and the incoming signal while that step is recording
Carries the current slot's playback at its gain unless that slot is muted, and the incoming signal while recording
Note — the sequencer has no clock of its own and moves only on the clock input or a step trigger, and only while it is running
Nova.notes: The panel prints Clear on the button and jack whose tooltips read Sequencer Reset; the code empties all eight sample buffers and leaves the sequencer where it is, so the panel is right and the tooltip is not.

lines: Clock pair: a gate called Alpha and a copy of it called Beta, shifted from it by anything up to a whole cycle, with a combined output as well
Sets the rate of both gates, 15 BPM at the bottom of its travel and 960 BPM at the top
Sets how far Beta is shifted from Alpha, 0 degrees at the bottom of its travel, 180 degrees at the middle and 360 degrees at the top
Sets how much of each cycle both gates stay high, from 1 per cent to 99 per cent
Every volt doubles the rate of both gates
Shifts Beta by 36 degrees per volt, a tenth of the knob's range
Carries a 10V gate whenever Alpha or Beta is high
Carries a 10V gate at the rate set by Alpha Rate
Carries a 10V gate at the same rate as Alpha, delayed by the amount set by Beta Shift
Eight-step rhythm generator: each step lasts for a time of its own and fires a chosen number of gates while it lasts, free running or counting an external clock
Sets how long that step lasts, as a percentage of the global rate
Sets how many gates that step fires, 1 to 32, spread evenly across the length of the step
Sets how long each of that step's gates stays high, as a percentage of the space between them
Sets how long a step of full length lasts, in decades from 0.01 seconds to 10000 seconds; with a clock patched, step lengths count clock pulses instead of seconds
Runs and stops the sequence
Steps the sequence direction on to the next of forward, reverse, bouncing and random
Adds to the length of that step, a tenth of the slider's range per volt
A rising edge advances the count, and patching anything here makes step and gate lengths count clock pulses rather than seconds
A rising edge sends the sequence back to its first step and restarts its timing
A rising edge runs or stops the sequence
A rising edge steps the sequence direction on to the next of forward, reverse, bouncing and random
Carries the 10V gates of that step while the sequence is on it, and 0V the rest of the time
Carries the gates of whichever step the sequence is on, at 10V
Botzinger.notes: The eight repeat CV jacks, inputs 8 to 15, are built and named but never read: the repeat count comes from the knob alone, so they are left untagged. The width CV inputs exist in the code with no jack on the panel. The maker's configOutput call in the loop omits its index, so only output 0 carries a tooltip name and the other seven are blank; all eight are step outputs.

lines: Eight-step Markov gate sequencer: on every clock pulse the next step is drawn at random, weighted by the eight knobs belonging to the step it is on
Sets the weight of one move: each column of knobs belongs to the step the sequence is on and each knob in it to a step that might come next, so the higher it is the likelier that move
A rising edge moves the sequence straight to that step, whatever the knobs say
A rising edge draws the next step and moves to it; the gate outputs stay high while this input is high, and nothing runs with nothing patched here
A rising edge starts the sequencer again after it has stopped
Carries a 10V gate while the sequence is on that step and the clock input is high
Note — when the eight knobs of the current step add up to less than 1, the remainder is the chance that the sequencer stops on the next clock pulse
Shaney.notes: Params 64 to 71 exist in the module but have no control on the panel and are never configured or read. The Run input carries no tooltip name because the maker's configInput call for it is missing; the panel prints Run.
